title: Programme
description: One word set two dozen times on a ruled grid, edge to edge in cells cut to its own proportion, black and one red on white, each cell a variant run by rule rather than drawn by hand. Two rows of a morphological box of typographic variables, weight, size, slope, rule, reversal, red and alignment, run along the columns and the rows. Drag across the grid to re-map which variables are running, and the whole grid recomposes in a wave from the hand, every cell interpolating its parameters. Click a cell to promote that variant to the chosen logotype; its edges step out along the rules, column by column and then row by row, until it is pasted in as a full-width band of the sheet over the cells it clears, holds, and returns.
intent: After Karl Gerstner's Designing Programmes (1964): design as a programme you can run, the morphological box of the typogram, and his grids of one logotype set across systematically varied parameters. https://medium.com/svilenk/what-i-learned-from-the-2-000-elusive-design-book-designing-programmes-f518faefcf4b. Tracking follows the house law at every rendered size, and resting weights come from the ladder tokens.
